reviews.review:
A great throwback to Left 4 Dead style gameplay. It's affordable enough to get a copy for a friend just to play for the weekend, and the bots are competent enough for when you're feeling antisocial.

A nice addition to the formula is "Matter Compilers" which allow you to pick one of 3 randomly selected perks that you get to take with you through the stages of the campaign chapter, changing gameplay significantly. A fully modded pistol with unlimited ammo or healing upgrade to grenades? They make big differences each time, especially when stacked with other perks.

Speaking of grenades, This game has some pretty creative grenades, like a vortex grenade that causes a black hole that sucks in aliens in a cool use of mass ragdoll physics, or a stasis grenade that creates a time dilation field that slows aliens caught inside to a near standstill.

Movement feels like a Source game. So much so that I thought it was a source game until I saw the Unreal logo. This isn't going to feature sprinting or mantling or sliding, but I don't need all that just to spend some time blasting aliens.

Good game, and a great value for the price.

Honestly it was a fun game.  Of course it's similar to Left 4 Dead but I think it's by far better than Back for Blood.  Feels like old school LFD and I'm not going to complain about that.  Don't listen to the reviews on youtube saying its a ripoff of LFD and the AI have no personality.  Most those reviews were playing on normal mode.  Intense mode is where it's at and the AI feel more up beat.  I'll definitely finish the campaign with my buddy.  Only thing I don't like is you can't private match with a friend and have to bot teammates.  Get ready to have random teammates that do not talk whats-so-ever.

While I've only played for roughly over an hour and finished just the first episode, I'd say this game is decent. It has some glaring issues, but its to be expected from a game in early access. Theres some goods, some greats, and some bads. For those expecting an experience similar to Left 4 Dead to play with friends and have fun, Anacrusis might be worth a try, but dont expect Anacrusis to be Left 4 Dead 3. 

The Good:
- The upgrade system in this game feels alright, doesn't distract the player away from the main objective and doesn't bog the player down with too many pregame choices, rather lets the player gradually build up their upgrades through upgrade machines scattered throughout.
- The aliens coming at the player in huge droves, while able to tank performance, is good at making the player feel overwhelmed and horded.
- The Brute is a decent alternative to the Tank. The Brute isn't a boss like the Tank, but is more like a mini-boss. The Brute doesn't make survivors change up their playstyle completely like the Tank does, but provides a big enough challenge that can make them just as dangerous. The Brute is faster than the Tank, but has what feels like significantly lower health, and can spawn more than once in a map.

The Great:
- The artstyle and general atmosphere of Anacrusis is amazing, genuinely enjoyed the calm moments where I was able to just look around and explore every little detail the maps had to offer.
- The characters, while at the moment lacking in prominent personalities, have a lot of potential, and I found myself enjoying each of them. I hope they're able to get fully fleshed out in the future.

The Bad:
- It is very easily to get confused on where to go, especially if it is your first time playing.
- Some moments have a seemingly endless horde, and to me it wasn't obvious that I should be running forward instead of sitting and holding my ground until half my teammates were dead, with the last two very very close to death.
- The Ai is a bit clunky and can be very very dumb at times, like leaving you for dead to go help someone else after they saved you from being grabbed.
- The flashlight is utilized very little.
- If you spend too much time not pushing forward or wandering around trying to find out where to go, the game will just path you to where you need to go. While a decent fix for now, this felt more like an annoyance and like the game was treating me like an idiot (which to be fair, I probably was).
- While the hordes being very massive is a good thing, it can also feel like there is way too many aliens, and often feels like you're just shooting into a wall if you have a very big crowd of them chasing after you. I would suggest downsizing the maximum amount of aliens that can exist at the same time, but keeping the amount that spawn for the overall horde the same.
- The Flasher is pretty well executed, but can very quickly become an egregious annoyance. Sometimes their flashing can go through walls when you'd normally not be able to see them.

The Confusing?:
- I'm not exactly sure what happened, but I apparently startled "The Egg" (I think thats what it said?) and these floating balls started chasing me.

What could be improved:
- The overall lighting could be adjusted. Maybe making areas that are off the main path darker than areas that are on the main path could help guide people who may be experiencing the game for the first time. Depending on the darkness level, it could also encourage players to use their flashlight to scavenge more effectively
- The weapons, while they feel good to shoot, don't exactly feel that powerful unless you go for a headshot and watch their heads pop. I would suggest a gore system, even a very simply and cartoonish one, but I think that would be outside the scope of the game.
- The blue guy with the tentacles, while having a slow charge up for his grabbing, pulls the survivors very quickly, and can lead to some frustration. I would suggest making his pull medium speed, and maybe decreasing his charge up time.

Overall, I think the early access has a ton of potential, and I can't wait to see what comes next. Hopefully all the issues that are indicative of an early access can be gradually ironed out to give a much better player experience. I'll play some more of it, and may adjust the review if my opinions change significantly.

This game falls very in-line with the L4D/L4D2 franchise, and many games alike as a 4-player apocalyptic-esque survival shooter. The developers, themselves, recognise the game similarities to the mentioned franchise, urging those that like those games to give it a try. The difference here is that the game doesn't try to be hyper-realistic and goes down a cartoon-y vibe with a retro 70's style which actually works amazingly and for the most part, looks like fun design. 

[u][h1]Pros:[/h1][/u]
- Mods: Maybe it's just my style of games that I pick out, but you don't often see too many games utilising the workshop feature on steam, which is a real DAMN shame (in of itself). The Anacrusis, however, DOES utilise this. Allowing players to have full customisation power over maps, cosmetics and challenges - which is a really nice touch to the game as it allows the community to keep the game alive, with it's creativity whilst adding endless replayability potential to the game. It's an awesome feature that you don't see much nowadays due to the industrial standard shifting towards F2P + Full Monetisation models so it feels refreshing to see modding as an option. 

- Player Diversity: There's obviously a higher demand in diversity, and the main cast are pretty diverse in their own right. Giving a fair chance for people to feel represented (Though of course, this could be improved on if they decide to introduce more characters down the line as there are currently only 4 choices). 

- Gameplay: As for how the game runs and feels, it is surprisingly smooth with very little issues. Considering that this game is still in early access, i was pleasantly surprised by how smooth it feels to move and shoot. 

- Free Battlepass (?): I initially got to play this game when it was free for a weekend, and purchased it after the deal ended. The game has a feature called 'Chapters', which looks as if it is just a battlepass, but there doesn't appear to be two tracks like in most game, but just one. You have about 15 Chapters, and to complete each chapter, you need to do 3 challenges which equals to 45 challenges, which is not too bad at all. Considering that the battlepass is not a paid feature, the content within it is satisfying, as it consists of titles, name banners, outfits, emotes, gun skins and gun buddies. I hope they reconsider splitting the 'Legendary' skins as they currently come in a bundle throughout the battlepass, and you can choose one skin per character, but it's only one bundle across the entire battlepass. 


[u][h1]Cons:[/h1][/u]

- Map Design: Generally, the maps are designed very well and I have no qualms. But there are specific areas within the maps that you can get stuck in and can't get out. This may be something that they fix considering that I've encountered areas like this mostly on EP4 - which at the time of this review is a BETA level and they may still be play-testing/fault finding things on this 3-levelled mission. But my suggestions for this, is to potentially add a climb feature into the game. 

- Side Missions: Generally, there isn't too much to change about them, other than one thing that feels slightly disappointing. I've played the game with friends so I've noticed that everyone's side missions are randomised, that's okay if it weren't for the fact that some missions feel really awkward and would generally prefer to see if this could be reworked. A lot of the challenges simply include killing aliens a certain amount or with a specific amount. But there are side missions that involve killing specific elites (Elites are like mini-boss aliens that have unique powers). Spawners and the Eggs sometimes feel a bit awful to get as a challenge as both Spawners and Eggs have a low spawn rate, and the Elites can also spawn in locations that are not accessible to the players, considering that the Eggs need to be 'awakened' for them to move and Spawners actively run away from players, if they spawn in those areas, it can almost feel as if you are being cheated, whilst everyone else around you is rushing through easier challenges that they get by RNG. 

[u][h1]Improvements/Suggestions:[/h1][/u]

- Character prefer system: There are only four characters, and you can only choose which character you prefer to play. If someone else in your lobby prefers that character, it dwindles down to RNG as to who gets that character. I think a better system would just be a first come, first serve or to allow duplicate characters in a lobby/mission. 

- Quickplay: There is an option for QP, and I am assuming that they received feedback on EP1 for being too long, because the later missions are no-where near as long. But the QP option just seems like a lobby joiner, where it will just throw you into the first match it finds. This can be fine if it's some of the later episodes but if you get EP1, that mission can easily last up to 50 minutes. QP should definitely be reworked to have smaller missions, or to prioritise lobbies that are closer to finishing as most people's idea of QP are matches that are 25 minutes MAX. 

- AI/AFK Pathing: Currently if you are playing with AI, their pathing is completely dependent on you as they will follow you around. I get what the devs were trying to do and actively avoid which is the AI getting stuck or refusing to come to the mission area. But I do think that AI should have a designated pathing that they closely follow which leads towards the mission area, with a loose following system of the players. As of right now, the AI have a tendency to steal items from under your nose, which can be pretty infuriating. 

[u][h1]Overall:[/h1][/u]
The game feels very smooth and easy to pick up - it follows a basic premise of a shooter with mostly easy and accessible controls. Any players of LFD2, or any other apocalyptic shooters will find themselves at home with this game, the idea/premise of the game sets it apart a bit as most games in this genre tend to opt for a zombie approach, whereas this game goes for a Retro/Futuristic 70s Alien break-out. There are little personal touches such as the game sequences being presented as a show, as if an audience is watching the players on a TV at home, with room for goofiness through emotes. 

In it's current state, the game is in early access and paying for it in full can feel a bit daunting. But as long as the developers. The developers do have a discord, which they seem to actively use and reply to people - especially with bug reports, and asking for volunteers for playtests. As long as they flesh out the game to it's potential whilst listening to the community, I think this game is worth purchasing and playing with friends as a fresh reset from old games. 

[u][h1]Final Rating:[/h1][/u]
7/10

I'll be brutally honest: this is probably the worst horde-shooter I've ever played. The maps are so boring, empty, and quiet. I remember maybe one song that played the entire time and it was during a horde that tanked me and my friend's fps to 30 even though this game looks like it was released in 2015. The special enemies are so ugly, janky, and nothing you probably haven't already seen before. One of them literally just blinds anyone in the entire room, like a walking sun. Another one seems like it can grab you at really any distance it feels like (sometimes grabbing me near a ledge and just dropping me to my instant death.) wow! This game had maybe 11 players before the f2p weekend, so don't expect a ton of workshop content to keep this game going. 

   There are literally 8 (9? honestly don't remember) guns in this game. Half of them being special pickups that have limited ammo. So you get a whopping FOUR guns to use (one of them is your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ infinite ammo pistol). But its fine because they can get random attachments on them! Except all they seem to really do is improve fire rate, reduce spread, or reduce recoil.  Nothing that seems to make the guns any more exciting. 

   Perks are also boring. I've only played 2 episodes out of 4 and I've just seen the same ones over and over. Half of them seem to just buff the shove (which by the way is on a pretty lengthy cooldown I think for a shove) which I never really ended up using and still never died the entire time. You can just press H to revive anyone who dies, any time, any where, so who cares? The other ones just buff your grenades or double your ammo capacity or I dont know, improve your gun in some meaningless way like smgs can now auto target enemies? Kind of? 

  If you click on the roadmap button on the main menu it takes you to a post from January 202[b]2[/b] saying how they want to leave early access by the end of the year. It is now January 2023, and I noticed episode 4 is still in VERY early beta and episode 5 isn't even in the game yet. Hm....

Sorry, but I wouldn't even be caught dead spending $10 on this game, let alone $30

This is a weird one. The good outnumbers the bad here, but the bad things seem very obvious in that they should have been addressed early. My biggest gripe is that there's no indicator as to where you should actually go. You just wander around these uniformly lit areas trying to find a random opening in the wall. 

The characters are okay enough, a bit more situational awareness in the dialogue would be nice but there's just enough to get by. 

There are some very odd design choices with the enemy characters too. You shoot something lying on the ground and it puffs up and starts rolling around the room chasing you? That definitely crossed the goofy boundary. You quickly lose character distinction when numerous enemies appear too. They just become weird shapes swarming around each other at points. 

Game play is fairly solid for what it is though. I like the weapon designs, and the most common alien type is satisfying to shoot for the most part. The bigger enemies start feeling papery though. Like you're shooting a big gun but you're getting no response when you hit these bigger enemies. No blood marks, no audible pain sound, it just dies randomly when it receives enough damage. 

Overall it was a positive experience but on a grading scale, I'd say it's resting around 75%. I'll recommend this but noting that you might be disappointed paying full price.
